To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ATB is a better predictor and mediator of intention than ATO; ATO has an indirect influence on intention through ATB; and the effects of ATO and ATB are moderated by the use of the previous version of the technology.
attitude toward using ICT (ATB) predicts intention to use ICT, while attitude toward ICT (ATO) predicts ATB, and ATO's influence on intention is mediated by ATB.
attitude toward using ICT as a behavior has a stronger impact on behavioral intention than attitude toward ICT, and attitude toward ICT has a positive influence over attitude toward using ICT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attitude in the ICT acceptance model.
the role of attitudes in ICT use and the relationships among different types of attitude and their effects on behavioral intentions.
the nature of attitudes toward ICT use and its impact on intention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

attitude toward ICT as a behavior has a direct and positive impact on behavioral intention, while attitude toward ICT as object has an indirect and positive effect on intention via its impact on attitude toward ICT as behavior.
attitude toward using ICT is the best predictor of behavioral intention, and it has a positive effect on attitude toward ICT.
ATO has a direct impact on ATB, which in turn has a positive effect on BI, which in turn predicts the actual technology usage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ATO is the most important antecedent to ATB, ATB has the strongest effect on intention, ATO has a significant impact on BI through ATB, and attitudes toward previous versions of the ICT are the strongest predictors of current attitudes.
the two types of attitudes are different constructs and should not be used interchangeably in research and practice.
attitude toward using ICT is an important predictor of intention and that attitude toward ICT and intention are reciprocally related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of attitudes in ICT acceptance and use should be carefully examined.
the two types of attitudes are different constructs and should be considered separately.
researchers should carefully distinguish the different attitude constructs and their roles and effects.
